name: Example Workflow
description: Template. Trigger: Chat. Flow: code -> condition -> loop(agent, save) -> code -> condition -> join; each condition follows a code step, never an agent or the loop. Route tokens use the reserved prefix example_route_, as in example_step.py, which is the webhook variant of the first step. The loop's max_iterations (5) equals the first step's item cap; the top-level max_iterations (10) is the workflow's own exported setting, separate from the loop's and not verified.

steps.name: Read the input
steps.code:
def handler(input: dict, ctx: dict) -> dict:
    # Stub (chat variant; example_step.py is the webhook variant). A real step reads the chat
    # attachment from ctx['input_dir']; uses email inputs only when trigger_name is 'Email'
    # and the attachment has the recorded shape; uses a webhook payload (sent <= 26,800
    # escaped bytes) only when its package_sha256 (full 64-hex SHA-256) verifies. It validates a
    # strict schema (unknown keys rejected at every level; reserved prefix 'example_route_'
    # rejected anywhere; campaign <= 100 chars; at most 5 locales = the loop's
    # max_iterations and 50 lines, counted first; locale codes, master not listed, no
    # duplicate locales; each line exactly id (letter first, unique), channel, field,
    # texts; visible text in every cell; no control characters in any string field;
    # unencodable or non-JSON data rejected first; each item <= 60 KB, all <= 200 KB),
    # calls its
    # tool once and writes report.json to
    # /workspace/example/<run_key>/.
    # Loop items: example_step.py builds {locale, lines: [{id, master, text}]}; a real
    # step adds 'checksum' (locale code + lines + rule findings). This stub pre-renders
    # 'lines' as text because the review agent's 'lines' input is a string.
    lines = '[L1] Hello => Hallo'
    locales = [{'locale': 'de-DE', 'lines': lines, 'checksum': '0123456789abcdef'}]
    return {'route': 'example_route_check', 'message': '', 'run_key': '0123456789abcdef',
            'report_checksum': '0123456789abcdef', 'locales': locales,
            'summary': 'example_route_check'}

child_steps.name: Save the review
child_steps.code:
def handler(input: dict, ctx: dict) -> dict:
    # Stub. Declares only small inputs (never the loop item). A real step validates run_key
    # and the locale with fullmatch, checks the review echoes the same checksum, strips
    # Content Translation's exact trailing leak (linear string operations, no regex; an
    # empty result -> check_incomplete), and writes
    # /workspace/example/<run_key>/reviews/<locale>.json as {data, checksum}, the data
    # carrying the locale checksum in its 'checksum' field. Its fallback writes nothing.
    return {'saved': True, 'summary': 'review saved'}
